title: Sync the open story with GitHub
prompt:
# Story: Sync the open story with GitHub

- **Story**: XXX-story-sync
- **Created**: 2026-11-28
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open a story, change it, save, press Sync and see the full screen with the files to upload; Sync now and open the pull request on
  GitHub; reopen and see the files waiting; merge it, change a linked driver on GitHub and see it come down by itself; make a conflict and
  see that nothing is done; Force pull and see the story replaced.

## Story

As a team member, I want to sync the story I am working on with GitHub from its bar, and see on one full screen what goes up, what comes
down and what blocks it, so that my team reviews my changes in a pull request and I always work on the latest version of the story and
the documents connected with it.

## Acceptance tests

The Sync button

- [ ] **Given** an open story and the project is connected to GitHub, **Then** the bar shows "Sync" with the refresh icon and the hint "Sync
  the project with GitHub".
- [ ] **Given** the project is not connected, **Then** Sync is disabled with the hint "Connect GitHub in Integrations first".
- [ ] **Given** the text of the story has unsaved changes, **Then** Sync is disabled with the hint "Save the story first".
- [ ] **While** a comparison or a sync runs, **Then** the icon spins.
- [ ] **Given** the last comparison found a conflict, **Then** the button has an amber dot named "Conflict with the base branch". **Given**
  it found files to download and no conflict, **Then** the dot is blue, named "Changes on the base branch".
- [ ] **When** the user presses Sync, **Then** the full screen opens and a comparison starts. Nothing is changed here or on GitHub until Sync
  now or Force pull is pressed.

The full screen

- [ ] **Given** the full screen is open, **Then** it covers the whole window above the builder, with the same layout as the diagram screen:
  a header with the branch icon, the title "Sync with GitHub", the line `<owner>/<repo> · <base branch> · <base folder or (root)>` and a
  close button; a row of documents; a body that scrolls; a footer with a status on the left and the actions on the right.
- [ ] **While** comparing, **Then** the body says "Comparing with <base branch>..."; **while** syncing, "Syncing...".
- [ ] **When** the user presses the close button, "Close" or Escape, **Then** the screen closes. **While** a comparison or a sync runs,
  **Then** the three are disabled.
- [ ] **Given** a request failed, **Then** the body shows its error.
- [ ] **Given** the repository is too large for GitHub to list in full, **Then** the body warns "The repository is too large for GitHub to
  list in full. Some files may be missing from this comparison."
- [ ] **Given** a comparison was made, **Then** the footer says "Compared with <base branch> at <short head SHA>", followed by "· Last
  synced <date and time>" when the project was synced before.

What takes part in the sync

- [ ] **Given** the comparison, **Then** the row shows the documents in this sync as chips, up to twelve and then "+N more", and the line
  "This story and the N documents connected with it: what it links to and what links to it. Other documents are left out. ADRs are always
  checked: new and changed ones come down, and one that is used goes up with this story."
- [ ] **Given** the story, **Then** its own files take part: `story.md`, `meta.json`, `diagrams/<kind>.mmd` and `ui.html`, in its folder
  whether it is in a theme or not.
- [ ] **Given** the story links to or derives from a document, or a document links to it, **Then** that document's files take part. A
  document that links to the story only on GitHub (in its `meta.json` there) is found too.
- [ ] **Given** any ADR, **Then** it is always compared: a new or changed one comes down. An ADR changed here goes up only when a document
  in this sync links to it. An ADR removed here is not brought back.
- [ ] **Given** a document that is not connected to the story, **Then** it is left out, even if it changed here or on GitHub.

The decision for each file

Each file is compared in three versions: here, on the base branch now, and on the base branch at the last sync.

- [ ] **Given** the file is the same here and on the base branch, **Then** nothing is done.
- [ ] **Given** the file changed on the base branch and not here, **Then** it is downloaded.
- [ ] **Given** the file changed here and not on the base branch, **Then** it is uploaded.
- [ ] **Given** the file changed here and was sent in a pull request that is still open, and the base branch did not change it, **Then** it
  is waiting for that pull request. **Given** the base branch did change it meanwhile, **Then** it is a conflict.
- [ ] **Given** the pull request it was sent in was merged, **Then** the version of the base branch is taken. **Given** it was closed
  without merging, **Then** it is forgotten and the file is uploaded again at the next sync.
- [ ] **Given** the file changed here and on the base branch, **Then** it is a conflict.
- [ ] **Given** a file exists only on GitHub because it was deleted here, **Then** it is left alone: deletions are not synced, except below.
- [ ] **Given** the story was moved to another theme folder here, **Then** its files in the old folder are deleted in the same pull request
  that adds them in the new one, unless they changed on GitHub since the last sync, which is a conflict.

What the body shows

- [ ] **Given** files to upload, **Then** a section "Upload N files as a pull request", with the hint "BWYN opens a new branch from <base
  branch> and a pull request. Review and merge it on GitHub." and their paths, relative to the base folder.
- [ ] **Given** files to delete, **Then** a section "Delete N files from the old folder", with the hint that the story was moved and that the
  same pull request adds it there and deletes it here.
- [ ] **Given** files to download, **Then** a section "Download N files from <base branch>" with their paths.
- [ ] **Given** files waiting, **Then** a section "N files are waiting for a pull request", with the hint "They come back in sync once the
  pull request is merged." and a link "Pull request #N" for each.
- [ ] **Given** nothing to do, **Then** "Everything is in sync with <base branch>."
- [ ] **Given** a comparison, **Then** "Details for each file" is folded at the end, listing each file with its decision and the short SHAs
  here (L), on the base branch now (R) and at the last sync (B).

A conflict stops everything

- [ ] **Given** at least one conflict, **Then** the body shows "Conflict with <base branch>. Nothing was changed.", the line "These files
  changed here and on <base branch>. Solve it on GitHub, by merging or updating the pull request, and sync again. Until then BWYN does
  nothing.", each file with an "Open" link to it on the base branch, and the pull requests waiting. No section of files shows.
- [ ] **Given** a conflict, **Then** Sync now is disabled, and nothing is downloaded or uploaded, not even the files without conflict.

Sync now

- [ ] **Given** no conflict and something to upload, delete or download, **Then** "Sync now" is enabled; otherwise it is disabled.
- [ ] **When** the user presses Sync now, **Then** the comparison is made again first. **Given** it now has a conflict, **Then** it is shown
  and nothing is done.
- [ ] **Given** no conflict, **Then** the files to download are downloaded and stored at once, replacing what is here, and the open story is
  shown from what was stored.
- [ ] **Given** files to upload or delete, **Then** the backend makes a new branch from the base branch with one commit and opens a pull
  request titled "BWYN: update N files of <project>" (with "and delete N files" when there are deletions), whose body lists the files and
  says "Review and merge this pull request on GitHub."
- [ ] **When** it is done, **Then** the body says "Synced", "N downloaded and saved, M uploaded.", the files that came down, the link "Pull
  request #N on <branch>" when one was opened, and any warning from reading the files (for example a `meta.json` that is not valid JSON).
  Sync now is hidden and the comparison is made again quietly.
- [ ] **Given** the sync worked, **Then** this project remembers the version of each file on the base branch and the files sent in each
  pull request, and the time of the sync.

Force pull

- [ ] **Given** a comparison with no result yet, **Then** the footer shows "Force pull" on the left of the actions, with the hint "Replace
  this story with its version on <base branch>, even when it clashes".
- [ ] **When** the user presses it, **Then** the footer's left side asks "Replace this story with the version on <base branch>? What you
  changed here is lost." with "Keep mine" and "Replace".
- [ ] **When** the user presses Replace, **Then** only the story's own files are downloaded and stored, whatever changed here, and the
  documents connected with it are not touched. A diagram that exists only here is kept. The body says "Replaced with the version on <base
  branch>" and the files that came down.
- [ ] **Given** the base branch has no file of the story, **Then** nothing is replaced and the body says "This story is not on <base
  branch>", explains that it was never merged there or was removed, and offers "Keep it here" and "Remove from here".
- [ ] **When** the user presses Remove from here, **Then** the story and its diagrams are deleted from this project (not from GitHub), what
  was remembered about its files is forgotten, and the screen closes.

Changes that come down by themselves

- [ ] **Given** an open story and a connected project, **Then** the head of the base branch is checked every 30 seconds, and also when the
  window gets the focus again.
- [ ] **Given** the head moved and the comparison finds files to download and no conflict, and the story has no unsaved changes, **Then**
  they are downloaded and stored, the story is shown from them, and a notice bar says "Updated from <base branch> and saved: <up to four
  files> and N more." Nothing is uploaded.
- [ ] **Given** the story has unsaved changes, **Then** nothing is downloaded and the notice says "A newer version of this document or its
  connected documents is on the base branch. Save or discard your changes and it is downloaded." When the story is saved, it is looked at
  again.
- [ ] **Given** a conflict, **Then** nothing is downloaded and the notice, in amber, says "The base branch has changes to this document or
  its connected documents that clash with yours. Nothing was changed. Solve it on GitHub, then sync."
- [ ] **When** the user dismisses the notice, or opens another document, **Then** it goes.

## Business rules and constraints

- **The rules are the spike's.** `classify` and `computePlan` in `syncEngine.ts` decide per file; this story does not change them.
- **The base branch is the source of truth.** BWYN never merges, never forces a push, and never solves a conflict: it is solved on GitHub.
- **One sync, one new branch and one pull request** from the base branch, named by the backend.
- **Deleting is not synced**, except the old folder of a story that was moved, in the same pull request that adds the new folder.
- **Downloads are stored at once**, like any change here, and the screen is rebuilt from what was stored.
- **Only the open story and the documents connected with it take part**, plus the ADRs.
- **One full screen component.** The sync screen uses the same layout as the diagram screen; extract the frame (header, legend row, body,
  footer) if it helps, but keep the two screens' contents apart.

## Out of scope

- A branch per story and "last push wins" (stories 2 and 3 of `story-document-bar-and-branch-sync.md`).
- Syncing the architectural enabler, drivers, architecture, runways and principles from this screen (they keep the dialog until they are
  moved to it).
- Choosing which files go up.
- Showing the difference of a file.
- Deleting a story on GitHub (the Delete button).

## Tasks

- [ ] Turn `SyncDialog` into a full screen with the frame of `DiagramDialog`: header, documents row, scrolling body, footer with the status
  on the left and Force pull, Close and Sync now on the right.
- [ ] Move the explanation of what is in scope under the documents row, and the Force pull confirmation into the footer's left side.
- [ ] Show "Compared with <base branch> at <SHA> · Last synced <date>" in the footer.
- [ ] Keep `SyncButton` (disabled reasons, spin, dots) and wire it to open the full screen.
- [ ] Keep `useGitSync`, `syncEngine`, `scope` and `gitClient` as they are, moving the remembered state from the browser to the project's
  database if it is not there yet.
- [ ] Test the screen for comparing, nothing to do, uploads, downloads, waiting, conflict, result, Force pull and "not on the base branch",
  and that Escape and Close are disabled while busy.

tasks.text: Move the remembered sync state (file SHAs, pull-request associations, last-sync timestamp) from browser storage to the project's database with a Flyway migration (ADR-0010, ADR-0011).

Add a backend application-service command and inbound REST adapter endpoint that accepts a list of files to upload or delete, creates a branch from the base branch, commits the files, and opens a pull request (ADR-0017).
Add a backend query endpoint that returns the current head SHA of the base branch and the status of open pull requests for the project (ADR-0017).

Refactor `SyncDialog` into a full-screen component sharing the frame layout (header, document-chip row, scrolling body, footer) with `DiagramDialog`; extract the frame only if a third screen already uses it (Principle: DRY and KISS) (ADR-0007, AE-0002).
Move the scope explanation line under the document-chip row and the Force pull confirmation into the footer's left side (ADR-0007).
Wire `SyncButton` (disabled states, spinner, amber/blue dots) to open the full screen and start a comparison (ADR-0007, AE-0002).

Implement the background polling hook (30-second interval plus window-focus trigger) that runs `classify`/`computePlan` and dispatches downloads or shows the notice bar without user action (ADR-0007, AE-0002).
Implement the "Sync now" flow: re-compare, download files atomically, call the upload/delete endpoint, update stored state, and rebuild the screen from stored data (ADR-0007).
Implement the Force pull flow: download only the story's own files, handle the "not on base branch" case with "Keep it here" / "Remove from here" (ADR-0007).

Write ViewModel unit tests for every comparison outcome (nothing to do, upload, download, waiting, conflict, moved-story deletion) and for the Sync now and Force pull flows, using test doubles for `gitClient` and the backend endpoints (ADR-0007, AE-0002).

Write React component tests for the full screen covering: comparing state, each body section, conflict state, result state, Force pull confirmation, "not on base branch" state, and that Escape and Close are disabled while busy (Principle: UI/Front end Tests pay only for what they assert).
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build).

Add a Flyway migration that keeps the time of the last sync with what the project knows of the branch of a document, and set it when a sync pushes or pulls (ADR-0010). _(`V26__remember_when_a_document_was_synced.sql`; set by `SyncDocumentCommandHandler` when it pushes or pulls.)_

Return with the comparison the head SHA it was made at, the time of the last sync, whether the repository listing was truncated, the repository and the base folder, and the details of each file of the story (path, what the sync does with it, SHA here, on the branch and at the last sync) (ADR-0017).

Turn the Sync dialog into a full screen with the frame of the diagram screen: header, scrolling body, footer with status and actions (ADR-0007). _(`SyncDialog` uses the `diagram-screen` classes of `DiagramDialog`; with two screens the frame is not yet extracted.)_
Spin the refresh icon of the Sync button while a comparison or a sync runs, and disable closing while busy (ADR-0007).
Show the footer status, the truncated warning and the folded "Details for each file" section (ADR-0007).
Write integration tests for the new fields of the comparison and the time of the last sync (ADR-0012). _(In `DocumentSyncIT`.)_

Write acceptance tests for the full screen: comparing and syncing states, the header line, the footer status, the truncated warning, the details section, closing disabled while busy, and the spinner (Principle: UI/Front end Tests pay only for what they assert). _(`sync-full-screen.acceptance.test.tsx`.)_
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build). _(`mvn verify` 5m07s plus Jest about 52 s on WSL.)_
